grh_6f68bc3075b52b9880fc.title: Magnificent Obsession
paragraphs: Reckless millionaire Robert Merrick nearly drowns, and the emergency equipment used to save him is therefore unavailable when beloved physician Dr. Hudson suffers a fatal accident. Hudsonâ€™s widow Helen resents Robert for the loss, and Robertâ€™s careless attempt to force a reconciliation contributes to another accident that leaves her blind. Haunted by the damage he has caused, Robert embraces the late doctorâ€™s ideal of quietly helping others, returns to medicine, and falls deeply in love with Helen. In Paris she learns his identity but also recognizes the man he has become; fearing that marriage to a blind woman would burden him, she leaves. grh_6f90d3c3505b114dd09c.title: The Case of the Out of Date Murder
paragraphs: Holmes visits museum curator Evan Whitlow after a body apparently dating from 1777 is found perfectly preserved in lime caves, but an anachronism in the dead man's supposed diary proves the corpse is modern. The victim is the long-missing George Clavering, whose disappearance had left his wife unable to move on with her life. Whitlow confesses that he killed George out of love for George's wife, then tried to pass the body off as an ancestor from the eighteenth century; jealousy deepened when he realized she loved George's brother Harry instead.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.d85c5443b80d8f78|The Adventure of Wisteria Lodge]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.
